article.headline: The Case for STMicroelectronics: Cycle, Factories, Terabits
article.lede: STMicroelectronics, the Franco-Italian chipmaker whose revenues fell roughly 32% from their 2023 peak, sits at the intersection of a classic semiconductor-cycle upturn, a company-driven manufacturing restructuring, and a nascent but growing position in AI infrastructure hardware. An investment thesis posted by @ContrarianCurse argues that sell-side models are underestimating all three forces — and are particularly slow to price in how quickly semiconductor gross margins recover once underutilised factories start filling up again.
article.body:
STMicroelectronics (STM) has spent two years at the bottom of one of the semiconductor industry's sharper downturns. Annual revenues fell from a $17.3 billion peak in 2023 to $11.8 billion by 2025, a decline of roughly 32% at the full-year level and closer to 40% when measured against the peak quarterly run-rate. **Gross margin** — the share of revenue remaining after manufacturing costs — compressed by approximately 14 percentage points, from nearly 48% at the cycle peak to around 34% by early 2026. The proximate causes were well documented: a bust in electric-vehicle semiconductor demand after years of overbooking, and a broad industrial *de-stocking cycle* in which customers ran down excess inventory rather than placing new orders. Capital expenditure, which peaked above $4 billion in 2023, fell to below $1.8 billion by 2025 — a cut of more than half.

The recovery mechanics here are standard for an *IDM* (integrated device manufacturer: a chipmaker that both designs and fabricates its own silicon) climbing off a trough. As factory *utilisation rates* rise toward normal levels, fixed manufacturing overhead spreads across more units, automatically lifting margins without any improvement in pricing. ST is also closing older, higher-cost facilities — a structural improvement that lifts gross margin independent of volume recovery. Inventory across the analogue semiconductor supply chain has been largely worked down, and *lead times* — the gap between order placement and delivery — have stabilised after a period of erratic compression. The analytically interesting variable is speed: cyclical margin recoveries in semiconductor IDMs tend to arrive faster than sell-side linear models anticipate. Bloomberg consensus reportedly places ST's gross margin at around 39% by 2028; the company's own target is 44–46% over the same window, a gap of five to seven percentage points that, closed a year early, would represent meaningful earnings upside against current expectations.

About half of ST's revenues come from automotive and industrial customers — the segments most exposed to the 2022–2024 de-stocking cycle. Early 2026 results, with Q1 revenues up 23% year-over-year, suggest those markets are normalising ahead of schedule. The remaining mix includes roughly 25% personal electronics and approximately 15% power semiconductors. Within personal electronics, Apple (AAPL) accounts for a verified **17.7%** of total group revenues, confirmed in the company's 2025 annual filing, making it ST's single largest customer. The thesis treats Apple as a relatively resilient consumer-hardware platform, with new product cycles across iPhone, AirPods, and Apple Watch providing more predictable demand than generic Android supply chains. Anchoring the microcontroller business is the **STM32** family of embedded processors, which has cultivated a developer community ST publicly describes as exceeding one million engineers. Embedded ecosystems carry high switching costs — certified firmware libraries, hardware abstraction layers, and toolchains accumulate over years and are rarely displaced.

The newer, potentially more transformative layer is ST's positioning in AI infrastructure. At the optical layer, ST's Crolles fab in France entered high-volume production of its *PIC100* *silicon photonics* process in March 2026 — a 300mm process capable of supporting transceivers running at 800 Gbps and scaling toward 1.6 Tbps, the bandwidth density required by next-generation AI *hyperscale* cluster interconnects. The broader Crolles expansion drew on €2.9 billion in approved French state aid under the *EU Chips Act*; the original partnership with GlobalFoundries (GFS) for a larger megafab has been paused following GlobalFoundries' withdrawal, though PIC100 production runs independently on the existing facility. On the power side, ST's *silicon carbide (SiC)* and *gallium nitride (GaN)* portfolio serves the *800V DC architecture* increasingly standard in both electric-vehicle powertrains and AI datacenter power delivery. At NVIDIA's (NVDA) GTC 2026 conference, ST was confirmed as an ecosystem partner in NVIDIA's 800 VDC reference design, supplying the complete conversion chain from 800V bus to GPU rail. Management has publicly guided for datacenter revenues exceeding $500 million in 2026 and surpassing $1 billion by 2027; analyst notes attribute approximately $230 million in component content per gigawatt of AI compute capacity built — a figure consistent with ST's guidance trajectory but not directly stated in primary press releases.

The bull case condenses into a timing question: how quickly do the cyclical recovery, the structural margin lift from factory rationalisation, and the AI revenue ramp compound together? The poster judges rival Infineon Technologies (IFX.DE), the Munich-based IDM with a near-identical automotive and industrial mix, to be pricing in a more optimistic recovery than STM — making ST the cheaper option on 2027 earnings estimates, with the photonics and power-AI exposure treated as incremental upside not yet fully reflected in consensus models. Material risks remain: the GlobalFoundries megafab delay removes one pillar of the original Crolles scale story; automotive and industrial recovery could stall on weaker macroeconomic conditions; and Apple's 17.7% concentration means any stumble in iPhone demand lands directly on ST's income statement. A potential EV revival driven by sustained higher fuel prices is acknowledged by the poster as a sentiment catalyst rather than a load-bearing assumption.

concepts.definition: A semiconductor company that both designs and manufactures its own chips, as opposed to a fabless designer (like Qualcomm) that outsources production or a pure-play foundry (like TSMC) that only manufactures. IDMs carry higher fixed costs but can optimise process technology precisely for their own products, and benefit from operational leverage when factories fill up.

The percentage of revenue remaining after deducting the direct cost of manufacturing — wafers, materials, and depreciation on fab equipment. In semiconductors it is the primary metric of pricing power and factory efficiency; utilisation rates have an outsized effect because manufacturing overhead is largely fixed regardless of how many chips come off the line.

The interval between when a customer places an order and when the supplier delivers it. In semiconductors, collapsing lead times signal excess inventory in the supply chain; rising lead times signal tightening supply and pricing power returning to the manufacturer. Stabilisation of lead times after a bust is an early indicator that the de-stocking cycle is ending.

A phase in which customers who over-ordered components during a period of scarcity work down excess inventory before placing new orders, causing a sharp drop in semiconductor revenue even if end-demand is steady. The 2022–2024 automotive and industrial de-stock was one of the deepest in recent history, a reversal of pandemic-era supply-chain panic-buying.

The percentage of a semiconductor factory's production capacity actually being used. When utilisation is low, fixed costs (equipment depreciation, cleanroom maintenance, labour) are spread over fewer chips, crushing gross margins. As utilisation recovers toward 80–90%, margins expand rapidly — this mechanical leverage is the core reason semiconductor earnings are so cyclically volatile.

A technology that builds optical components — lasers, modulators, photodetectors, and waveguides — on standard silicon wafers using adapted CMOS manufacturing processes. It enables high-bandwidth, low-power optical data links at semiconductor cost and scale, critical for AI cluster interconnects that must move petabits of data between GPU racks inside and between datacenters.

STMicroelectronics' first proprietary silicon photonics process technology, manufactured on 300mm wafers at its Crolles fab in France. It entered high-volume production in March 2026 and supports optical transceiver modules operating at 800 Gbps today, with a roadmap extending to 1.6 Tbps aggregate bandwidth — the scale required by next-generation AI hyperscale datacenters.

A wide-bandgap semiconductor material that handles higher voltages, higher temperatures, and higher switching frequencies than conventional silicon. Dominant in electric vehicle traction inverters and increasingly used in high-voltage datacenter power supplies, SiC is harder and more expensive to manufacture than silicon, creating meaningful barriers to entry for qualified suppliers.

Another wide-bandgap semiconductor, better suited than SiC for very high switching frequencies at moderate voltages. Used in compact, high-efficiency power adapters, server power supplies, and RF devices. GaN enables power converters that are physically smaller and more efficient than silicon alternatives at the same voltage level.

An 800-volt direct-current power bus standard adopted in next-generation electric vehicles and AI datacenters. In EVs it enables faster charging and lighter cabling; in datacenters it reduces conversion losses from utility power to the GPU rail. It requires wide-bandgap semiconductors (SiC or GaN) that can safely switch at these voltages, which is why it creates a structural demand tailwind for suppliers like STMicroelectronics.

A €43 billion European Union framework, passed in 2023, designed to double Europe's share of global semiconductor production from roughly 10% to 20% by 2030. It provides state-aid exemptions for first-of-a-kind advanced fabrication facilities; STMicroelectronics received €2.9 billion in approved French state aid under the act for its Crolles expansion, and a separate €2 billion in Italian state aid for its Catania silicon carbide facility.

STMicroelectronics' family of 32-bit ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers, among the most widely deployed embedded processors globally. Used in industrial automation, consumer electronics, IoT devices, automotive subsystems, and medical equipment. The surrounding ecosystem of development tools, certified firmware libraries, and reference hardware creates high switching costs that make the installed base durable across semiconductor cycles.

Refers to the very largest cloud and AI infrastructure operators — Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Meta — that build and operate datacenters at a scale of tens of thousands of servers and hundreds of megawatts of power. Their procurement decisions move entire semiconductor markets, and a design win with a single hyperscale customer can be worth hundreds of millions in annual revenue to a component supplier.

article.fact_check: Three claims in the tweet merit scrutiny. First, 'revs down 40%': on an annual basis the decline from the 2023 peak to the 2025 trough was roughly 32%; 40% is approximately accurate only when comparing peak quarterly run-rates, and is mildly overstated on the most standard full-year basis. Second, '1.5m devs': STMicroelectronics publicly cites its STM32 developer community as exceeding one million; the specific 1.5 million figure could not be verified in primary sources, though it is broadly consistent with reported ecosystem growth trends. Third, '17x 27 numbers': at the stock's approximate May 2026 price of roughly $59, dividing by 2027 consensus EPS of approximately $2.43 yields around 24x — not 17x. The poster may have written the thesis when the stock was trading near $41 (at which price 17x $2.43 holds), or may be using a more conservative earnings estimate than consensus; without knowing the timing and entry price, the valuation framing cannot be fully assessed from the tweet alone. Additionally, the tweet implies GlobalFoundries remains an active co-builder of the Crolles photonics facility; in fact, GlobalFoundries paused participation in the larger megafab project in 2025, and PIC100 production is running independently on ST's existing 300mm facility.

ticker_stm.name: STMicroelectronics N.V.
ticker_stm.blurb: STMicroelectronics is a global semiconductor group covering microcontrollers, sensors (MEMS), and — most relevant to the AI power-plumbing thesis — a broad power-semiconductor portfolio spanning SiC MOSFETs (STPOWER Gen 4), GaN devices, silicon IGBTs, and power-management ICs. ST is one of only a handful of vendors with an end-to-end 800 VDC power-conversion solution for AI data centres, offering complete reference designs from 800V bus-to-50V, 12V, and 6V conversion using its own SiC and GaN silicon. The company serves automotive, industrial, and, increasingly, hyperscale data-centre customers.
ticker_stm.recent: ST reported Q1 2026 revenue of $3.10 billion, up 23% year-over-year and above consensus of $3.04 billion, with Q2 2026 guidance of ~$3.45 billion. In March 2026 the company announced expanded 800 VDC power-conversion products (12V and 6V architectures) developed to the NVIDIA 800 VDC reference design and showcased at NVIDIA GTC 2026. In February 2026 ST disclosed a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar engagement with Amazon Web Services to supply semiconductors for AWS compute and AI data-centre infrastructure. Management projects data-centre revenue exceeding $500 million in 2026 and surpassing $1 billion in 2027.

ticker_aapl.name: Apple Inc.
ticker_aapl.blurb: Apple designs and markets consumer electronics (iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch), software, and digital services. The iPhone remains the dominant revenue driver, but the Services segment — comprising the App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, Apple Pay, and licensing — has grown into a high-margin business that Wall Street values separately. Apple commands one of the highest brand loyalty rates in consumer technology and operates a tightly integrated hardware-software ecosystem.
ticker_aapl.recent: Apple reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $400 billion. The company has faced headwinds from slowing iPhone upgrade cycles in mature markets and regulatory pressure on App Store commissions in both the US and EU. Apple Intelligence, its generative AI suite, launched in late 2024 but has not yet materially re-accelerated upgrade cycles. Paul Pelosi sold 45,000 shares of AAPL according to the January 2026 PTR disclosure — the largest single sale in the filing by share count.

ticker_gfs.name: GlobalFoundries Inc.
ticker_gfs.blurb: GlobalFoundries Inc. (NASDAQ: GFS) is the world's third-largest semiconductor foundry by revenue, operating advanced manufacturing facilities in the United States (Fab 8 in Malta, NY; Vermont), Germany (Dresden), and Singapore. Unlike TSMC and Samsung, GlobalFoundries exited the leading-edge node race in 2018 and now focuses on differentiated specialty processes: silicon photonics, silicon-germanium (SiGe), RF CMOS, FD-SOI (fully depleted silicon-on-insulator), and embedded non-volatile memory. This positions GF as a complement — and sometimes a competitor — to Tower Semiconductor in the specialty foundry space.
ticker_gfs.recent: GF reported FY2025 revenue of $6.79 billion (up 1% year-over-year) with gross margin improving 360 basis points to 29% and diluted EPS of $1.72. Silicon photonics revenue exceeded $200 million in 2025 and is expected to nearly double in 2026, with management guiding toward a $1 billion annual run rate by end-2028. In June 2025, the company announced a $16 billion US investment plan anchored by its New York and Vermont fabs. GF also finalised a $1.5 billion CHIPS Act direct-funding agreement with the US government. In January 2026, GF agreed to acquire Synopsys' ARC Processor IP unit, targeting physical-AI embedded applications.

ticker_nvda.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ticker_nvda.blurb: NVIDIA designs graphics processing units (GPUs) and system-on-chip products. Originally a gaming chip company, it became the dominant supplier of AI accelerators — chips that perform the parallel matrix math required to train and run large language models. Its H100, H200, and Blackwell GPU families are the de facto standard for AI training infrastructure at hyperscalers and cloud providers. NVIDIA's CUDA software ecosystem creates deep switching costs: virtually all AI frameworks and models are optimised for CUDA, making competing hardware difficult to adopt at scale. NVIDIA also sells networking (InfiniBand, Ethernet) and data-centre systems.
ticker_nvda.recent: NVIDIA reported FY2026 (ending Jan 2026) revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% YoY, with data centre revenue reaching $186 billion. The company's forward P/E of ~17.5x on 34.8% projected EPS growth produces a PEG of 0.50 — unusually cheap for what is arguably the most critical infrastructure company in the AI buildout. Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) collectively committed over $200 billion in AI infrastructure capex for 2026, the majority flowing through NVIDIA's supply chain.

ticker_ifx-de.name: Infineon Technologies AG
ticker_ifx-de.blurb: Infineon Technologies AG is a German semiconductor manufacturer that provides microelectronics solutions for automotive, industrial, and security applications. The company is a leading supplier of power semiconductors and microcontrollers, particularly for electric vehicles and renewable energy systems. Infineon operates globally with a strong market position in the automotive and industrial sectors.
ticker_ifx-de.recent: In the past 30 days, Infineon's stock has shown moderate volatility amid broader market trends. The company released its Q1 fiscal 2025 earnings, reporting revenue of €3.4 billion, slightly above expectations, driven by strong demand in automotive and green energy segments. Analysts have maintained a positive outlook on the stock due to its exposure to electrification and decarbonization trends.
